title: Operational stability roadtrip: stakeholder bridge & sprint itinerary
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic 6-week 'roadtrip' plan to align cross-functional partners on a set of service-level objectives for our model-serving surface, with an emphasis on fast feedback loops, minimally invasive experiments, and a clear handoff to feature teams and SRE ops. Think field itinerary not a fully-baked program spec — usable during stakeholder visits, war-room sessions, and pairing days.

Scope & audience:
- Scope: hosted API (text generation + chat + embeddings) + Dedicated pools that support customer tenants. Excludes Private on-prem packaging (separate engagement).
- Audience: product owners for Hosted API, eng leads for Serving Runtime, Platform, SRE oncall leads, Console/Product analytics, Solutions Eng.

High-level objectives (measurable):
- Define/reach consensus on 3 primary SLOs for Q2 pilot (availability, p99 generation latency, embedding throughput latency).
- Run at least 3 quick experiments that validate telemetry & alerting for p99 tail and cache effectiveness.
- Produce one concise runbook and one rollout gating checklist per SLO.
- Handoff: product teams can adopt SLOs as acceptance criteria in next release.

Success metrics (how we know this worked):
- Stakeholder sign-off on canonical SLO definitions (documented in Confluence).
- Synthetic canary generated with <10% end-to-end variance vs baseline for 72h.
- Two regressions caught by new quality checks before user impact.
- Runbook passed basic tabletop and two oncall responders can execute it.

6-week itinerary (field-style):
Week 0 — Pack & prep (Jan 15–21)
- Prep artifact pack: current dashboards (p50/p90/p99), traffic profiles, KV cache hit rate, batching stats, cost per token by model. (Owner: Evan)
- Create Slack channel #ops-roadtrip and invite PO, SRE leads, Solutions Eng, Product Analytics. (Owner: Jordan)
- Quick stakeholder survey: 5 Qs about pain points and non-negotiables. (Owner: Priya)

Week 1 — Discovery hop (Jan 22–28)
- Day 1: 90m sync with Hosted API PO + console analytics — align product goals and any contract/market constraints.
- Day 2: Pair with Serving Runtime to review common failure modes and perf knobs (batching windows, KV cache TTL).
- Day 3: Run short synthetic workload to capture baseline p99 with current autoscaling config (ticket ENG-FT-1047).
- Outputs: baseline dashboard snapshot, list of instrumentation gaps.

Week 2 — Define SLOs & guardrails (Jan 29–Feb 4)
- Workshop: propose SLOs (draft below). Rapid polling during workshop for each stakeholder.
- Draft rollback/fallback policies for cases where SLOs cannot be met at scale.
- Produce release gate checklist for canary. (Owner: Marisa)

Week 3 — Rapid experiments (Feb 5–11)
- Experiment A: KV cache hit-rate boost — tighten TTL on low-variability requests, monitor error/latency delta. (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/changes/exp-cache-ttl)
- Experiment B: Reconfigure batching policy for 99th percentile reduction (smaller max batch + priority fast-path).
- Experiment C: Synthetic spike test for routing fallback (route to cheaper quantized variant under stress).
- Each experiment: 48–72h run, daily check-ins, immediate abort criteria documented.

Week 4 — Canary & runbook drafting (Feb 12–18)
- Canary run for chosen SLOs across 3 traffic slices (low, median, tail). Collect ticketed anomalies.
- Draft runbooks: detection, triage checklist, mitigation actions (scale, route, degrade quality gracefully).
- Tabletop: 60m runbook walkthrough with oncall responders.

Week 5 — Handoff & triage rehearsal (Feb 19–25)
- Handoff pack to feature teams: canonical SLOs, dashboard, runbook, rollback playbook.
- Rehearse an injected incident (simulated cache loss) and practice runbook steps. Capture play-by-play.
- Finalize decisions for productionizing SLOs (policy doc + tickets).

Key proposed SLO drafts (workshop starting point):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful request rate (2xx) per rolling 30d for hosted generation endpoints; exclude maintenance windows and scheduled model swaps.
- Latency SLO (generation): p99 tail under 600ms for small prompt generation (<=128 tokens) on hosted-1 tier; note: p90 and p50 targets separate for product KPIs.
- Embedding latency: p95 under 120ms for single-embedding requests from eu-west region.
- Quality guard: For model variant fallbacks, measure immediate semantic drift rate on eval prompt set and require <5% drop vs baseline; otherwise route to safe-fallback + alert.

Stakeholder bridge map (quick):
- Hosted API PO — Priya Patel — product acceptance, pricing constraints, customer SLAs.
- Serving Runtime — Evan Chen — knobs, kernel selection, batching changes.
- Platform Eng — Theo Alvarez — capacity reservations, Dedicated pool policy, autoscaling overrides.
- Product Analytics — Marisa Gomez — define measurement windows, dashboards, alert thresholds.
- Solutions Eng — Lydia Shaw — customer impact and rollout communication.

Communication & cadence:
- Daily 15m standup during experiment weeks in #ops-roadtrip (check progress, abort signals).
- Weekly 60m sync for cross-team decision-making (Tues 11am PT).
- Brief weekly digest with 3 bullets: wins, regressions, asks.

Runbook skeleton (to iterate in Week 4):
1) Alert trigger — source/metric, threshold, and initial severity.
2) Quick triage checklist — recent deployments, autoscaler events, infra throttles, model swaps.
3) Mitigation steps — scale up pool, switch routing policy, disable batching optimization, revert model variant.
4) Communication template — SLACK + Incident bridge message + customer-facing note draft.
5) Postmortem prompts — impact scope, RCA owners, remediation backlog.

Risk matrix (top items):
- Risk: SLO too strict for early capacity (impact: false positives, alert fatigue). Mitigation: staged thresholds + error budget burn rate monitoring.
- Risk: Quality regressions when routing to quantized/cheaper variants. Mitigation: small eval set run on every rollout and automatic rollback if drift > threshold.
- Risk: Observability gaps (missing p99 breakdown by model). Mitigation: patch tracing/metrics collection early in Week 1.

Quick experiments (detailed probes):
- Probe: tail-latency census — add synthetic clients at various sizes to reproduce p99 and collect kernel-level metrics. Owner: Evan. Ticket: ENG-4912.
- Probe: KV cache TTL heatmap — change TTL per prefix class and measure percent reduction in compute RUs. Owner: Marisa.
- Probe: batching cold start test — inject low-QPS long-context sequences to see batching degradation. Owner: Theo.

Open questions / decisions to surface in Week 1 workshop:
- Which customer-facing SLA level do we commit to for early adopters on Dedicated? (pricing + legal consult)
- How do we handle multi-model requests for SLO accounting (single request hitting multiple model families)?
- What is the canonical window for SLOs (rolling 30d vs 7d for experiments)?

Tickets & immediate next steps (minimum viable backlog):
- ENG-FT-1047: baseline synthetic run + dashboard snapshot (Owner: Evan)
- ENG-FT-1048: instrument p99 by model and route (Owner: Marisa)
- ENG-FT-1051: runbook template + initial tabletop (Owner: Jordan)
- ENG-FT-1052: experiment gating checklist + abort criteria (Owner: Priya)

Notes to self / field scribbles:
- Keep experiments small and reversible — prefer 'knobs' over code changes where possible.
- When in doubt run pairing session on call with SRE and runtime engineer — faster alignment.
- Save concrete examples of customer impact to show execs (one pager).

Appendix: quick checklist for tabletop readiness:
- Does the runbook list a clear detection metric and owner? Y/N
- Do we have a synthetic canary config? Y/N
- Is there a rollback path that does not require infra change? Y/N
- Are runbook steps actionable by two oncall engineers within 15 minutes? Y/N

——
This doc is intentionally portable: copy the itinerary into your calendar for pairing days and use the quick experiments as fallbacks if the team prefers small, fast wins. Replace placeholders (ENG- tickets / Confluence urls) with the canonical IDs during Week 0 prep.
